{{Short description|German mathematician (1898–1944)}}
'''Gerhard Karl Theodor Haenzel''' (5 March 1898, [[Wolin (town)|Wolin]], [[Pomerania]] ([[German Empire]]) – 6 March 1944, [[Lesneven]], [[Brittany]] ([[German military administration in occupied France during World War II|occupied France]])) was a German mathematician.

==Education and career==
Haenzel, whose father was a teacher and school board member, completed his ''[[Abitur]]'' after studying from 1907 to 1915 at the Peter Gröning-Gymnasium in [[Stargard]]. Shortly after his ''Abitur'', he was called up in July 1915 for active military service. His military service lasted until 30 September 1920 and he attained the rank of lieutenant. He was on the Eastern and Western fronts and in the German fight against the [[Greater Poland uprising (1918–1919)|Polish uprising]]. He suffered a serious wound and was awarded the Iron Cross 1st and 2nd class.<ref name=Muenster>{{cite web|title=Prof. Dr. Ing. Dr. rer. nat. Gerhard Haenzel (1898 — 1944)|website=Ehemhalige Profeesoren (uni-muenster.de)|pages=96–99|url=https://www.uni-muenster.de/FB10/historie/NEU%20Ehemalige%20Professoren%201773%20-%201945.pdf}}</ref> From 1920 to 1925 he studied mathematics and physics at the ''[[Technische Universität Berlin|Technische Hochschule Berlin]]'' (TH Berlin) and then worked there successively as an assistant to the mathematician [[Georg Hamel]], then to {{ill|Stanislaus Jolles|de}}, and finally to {{ill|Erich Salkowski|de}}.<ref name=NDB>{{cite journal|author=Reutter, Fritz|title=Haenzel, Gerhard|journal=Neue Deutsche Biographie|volume=7|publisher=Duncker & Humblot|location=Berlin|year=1966|ISBN=3-428-00188-5|page=447|url=https://www.deutsche-biographie.de/gnd125021992.html#ndbcontent}}</ref> In 1926 Haenzel received his engineering doctorate with dissertation ''Zur synthetischen Theorie der Mechanik starrer Körper''<ref>{{cite journal|author=Haenzel, Gerhard|title=Zur synthetischen Theorie der Mechanik starrer Körper|journal=Sitzungsberichte der Berliner Mathematischen Gesellschaft|volume=26|year=1927|pages=126–162}}</ref> (On synthetic theory of the mechanics of rigid bodies) under the supervision of Stanislaus Jolles at TH Berlin. There Haenzel completed in 1929 his [[habilitation]]<ref>{{cite journal|author=Haenkel, Gerhard|title=Theorie und Klassifikation der Kollineationen vermöge der Involutionen auf der linearen Strahlenkongruenz|journal=Tohoku Mathematical Journal|series=First Series|volume=31|year=1929|pages=388–419|url=https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/tmj1911/31/0/31_0_388/_article/-char/ja/}} (Theory and classification of the collineations by involution on the linear congruence of rays; habilitation thesis)</ref> under the supervision of Erich Salkowski. From 1929 to 1933 Haenzel worked as a ''[[Privatdozent]]'' at TH Berlin.<ref name=NDB/>

In 1933 he was appointed a professor of geometry (as successor to [[Richard Baldus]]) at the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology|''Technische Hochschule Karlsruhe'']] (TH Karlsruhe). In 1936 he was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Oslo.<ref>{{cite book|author=Haenzel, Gerhard|pages=51–52|volume=Tome II|chapter=Neue Eigenschaften der linearen Strahlenkongruenz|title=Comptes rendus du Congrès international des mathématiciens, Oslo 1936}}</ref> Haenzel did research on [[algebraic geometry]] and the relationships between geometry and physics. In 1937 he was appointed to the professorial chair for mathematics and mathematical technology at TH Karlsruhe. Of particular interest is his research revealing the equivalence of the structure of the operators of the Dirac wave equation with various configurations of projective geometry and line geometry, as well as the [[icosahedral group]]. In 1940 he received the post-graduate degree [[Dr. rer. nat.]] from the [[University of Freiburg]] with a thesis on geometry and [[Schrödinger equation|wave mechanics]]<ref name=NDB/> under the supervision of [[Wilhelm Süss]].<ref name=Muenster/> In 1943 Haenzel resigned from TH Karlsruhe and accepted a professorial chair in mathematics at the [[University of Münster]].<ref name=NDB/> Soon after, he was drafted into military service. He committed suicide in Brittany. According to Max Pinl, his death in occupied France was due to pressure from the political intrigue of a court-martial in Lesneven.<ref>Max Pinl ''Kollegen in einer dunklen Zeit'', Part 3, Jahresbericht DMV, vol. 73, 1972, p. 204</ref>

==Selected publications==
* ''Ein neuer Satz über die Nullstellen ganzer rationaler Funktionen,'' Sitzungsberichte Berliner Mathematische Gesellschaft, vol. 27, 1928, pp.&nbsp;17–19
* ''Über die charakteristischen Involutionen der nicht-euklidischen Bewegungen'', Monatshefte für Mathematik, vol. 37, 1930, pp.&nbsp;209–214
* ''Über eine Klasse von Abelschen Gleichungen'', Jahresberichte DMV, vol. 41, 1931, pp.&nbsp;39–47
* ''Über die zeitlich veränderliche Metrik'', Monatshefte f. Math. und Physik, vol. 39, 1932, pp.&nbsp;267–278
* ''Über Lösungen der Gravitationsgleichungen Einsteins'', [[Zeitschrift für Physik]], vol. 72, 1931, pp.&nbsp;798–802 {{doi|10.1007/BF01342001}}
* ''Euklidische Geometrie, nichteuklidische Geometrie und Raum-Zeit-Struktur im System Spinozas'', Sitzungsberichte Berliner Mathem. Gesellschaft, vol. 31, 1932, pp.&nbsp;55–67
* ''Eine geometrische Konstruktion der transfiniten Zahlen Cantors'', Journal f. Math., vol. 170, 1934, pp.&nbsp;123–128 {{doi|10.1515/crll.1934.170.123}}
* [https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/tmj1911/43/0/43_0_33/_article/-char/ja/ ''Nichteuklidische Geometrie und ihre Verwendung in der Physik''], Tohoku Math. Journal, vol. 43, 1937, pp.&nbsp;169–181
* ''Geometrie und Wellenmechanik'', Parts 1,2,3, Jahresbericht DMV, [https://eudml.org/doc/146224 Part I], vol. 49, 1939, pp.&nbsp;215–242; [https://eudml.org/doc/146254 Part II], vol. 50, 1940, pp.&nbsp;121–129; [https://eudml.org/doc/146304 Part III], vol. 52, 1942, pp.&nbsp;103–117
* ''Die Diracsche Wellengleichung und das Ikosaeder'', Journal f. Math., vol. 183, 1941, pp.&nbsp;232–242 {{doi|10.1515/crll.1941.183.232}}
* [https://mas.goetheanum.org/fileadmin/mas/downloads/Mathematik/201910_Werk_HaenzelGerhard/30_deBroglie_Theorie_des_Photons.pdf ''Die Brogliesche Theorie des Photons in geometrischer Darstellung''], Zeitschrift für technische Physik, vol. 24, 1943, pp.&nbsp;87–90
